panels.description: Wide, full width. Wet sand at low tide, hard morning glare. Nagoji on his plain grey gelding, in his commander kit (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar at his hip; thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN), stands in his stirrups, one arm flung out, mouth open in a shout. Ahead of him a ragged double line of riders: tall Madurai chargers beside small shaggy Maravar ponies, the line bowing where the ponies cannot keep pace. Beyond them, Kerala plank-sewn fishing canoes and log catamarans drawn up in the shallows, fishermen watching from them, one doubled over laughing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Months of sun and salt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I became, in a small way, part of the landscape.

panels.description: Small inset, lower corner of 1.1. Evening in a thatched fisherman's hut. A banana-leaf plate of red fish curry, a coconut-shell cup of toddy, and above them Nagoji's face: eyes watering from the chilli, mouth open, fanning his tongue with one hand, grinning in spite of himself. A fisherman beside him laughing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Spicy enough to make a Deccan man weep for milk.

panels.description: Wide. Inland now. A narrow earthen bund between flooded paddy fields, green and mirror-bright. Nagoji's mounted column comes along it in single file at full gallop: Nagoji at the head on his plain grey gelding, rust-red turban, talwar drawn; behind him Madurai lancers in bright high-wrapped turbans and Maravar riders in white mundus hitched for riding and short jackets. At the far end of the bund, a knot of chavers on foot turns toward the sound: Nair fighters, bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, ash smeared on chest and brow, swords and small round shields. Behind them an official in a white mundu and shoulder cloth kneels on the bund, hands raised. Shoot from low at the waterline so the horses loom. No contact yet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But the king did not keep me only on the beach.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Small wars that never reached European maps, but decided who paid tax and who held a temple key.

panels.description: Dusk. The column returning along a village road, fewer riders than before. Nagoji at the head on his plain grey gelding, rust-red turban, not turning around. Riders with bandaged forearms, one arm in a sling, clean cloth, no blood; a riderless horse led by its reins. The Madurai and Maravar riders behind him are watching his back, not the road.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We came back with a different kind of silence.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kind that forms when soldiers have watched you ride into danger instead of pointing at it from behind.

panels.description: Bottom strip. A palace verandah at the roadside. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) sits at the verandah's edge with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Nagoji, rust-red turban, has reined in his plain grey gelding at the verandah's edge beside him, level with him, while the rest of the column files past behind. Ramayyan does not raise his eyes from the leaf.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Maharaja has seen you in blood, not only in sand.

panels.description: Wide establishing. A small open pavilion of dark oiled wood beside a temple wall, the temple's copper-clad flagmast and tiered sloping roofs rising behind it as background only. Nagoji (rust-red turban) steps up into the pavilion barefoot, his boots left at the pavilion step, a folded palm-leaf ola in his hand. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth), a minister at his accounts and not a priest, sits cross-legged at a low desk, bundles of palm leaves stacked at his knee, stylus moving. No ritual implements, no lamp, no offering plate. He does not look up.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then the king's ola came. Not to the war hall.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The King is pleased with the sand. He thinks you might be useful indoors as well.

panels.description: Two-shot across the low desk. Nagoji standing, barefoot. Ramayyan still writing.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I prefer the sky.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Preferences are luxuries. There is an estate that can house you and your officers. Padmini Amma's lands.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The woman who owned pepper hills.

panels.description: Close on Ramayyan as he finally looks up, the stylus paused above the leaf.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His gaze was like a clerk's scale, weighing gold against brass.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: She is Nair. Her house follows the old ways. They are... particular about who sleeps under their roof.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are Maratha? Which line?

panels.description: Nagoji, square to him, chin up. Shot slightly from below.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Sawant. Kshatriya. My father's house has held the sword for five generations.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We do not plough.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In this land, as in mine, questions of blood and birth could close a door faster than any bolt.

panels.description: Ramayyan already back at his leaf. Tight on the stylus scratching a line into the palm leaf, his face beyond it, finished with the matter.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Good. That will satisfy the temple priests who cook at her house.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Padmini Amma might tolerate a foreign captain, but she will not tolerate pollution.

panels.description: Large, top half of the page. Seen from the approach road under the palms: the estate house, sprawling low and wide, its roofs of curved hand-made country clay tiles, weathered dark, sloping gently in several tiers, carved beams dark with oil and age, a long compound wall. Two great tuskers sway in the shade of that wall, grey as boulders. A long stable runs off to one side. Small in the foreground, on horseback: Nagoji (rust-red turban) on his plain grey gelding, and Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat) on his sturdy brown pony. No women in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first time I saw Padmini Amma's house, I thought they had brought me to a temple by mistake.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not one of the great stone temples of the Deccan. Yet everything about it said power.

panels.description: Riding in under a gate arch woven from coconut fronds and mango leaves. Oil lamps hang in it, lit although the sun is high, thin smoke curling from the wicks. Ibrahim on his sturdy brown pony (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, shorter than the fishermen but broader, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, a scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw) leans toward Nagoji (rust-red turban, on his plain grey gelding) as they pass under.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Do not look for the sardar. Here the house does not belong to the man who sleeps in the front room.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: It belongs to the name on the mother's line. You will see.

panels.description: Inside the outer yard. A thick-walled granary, its door open on mounds of paddy stacked high. Beyond it, men with spears stand not at the gate but in the cool shade of an inner verandah, easy and watchful. No principal in frame.

Inset, tight, in the shadow of the granary wall. A low wooden panel set into the wall, plain, its edges rubbed smooth and darker than the wood around them, as if hands have found it in the dark many times. No figure in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It looked like nothing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That was what made it feel important.

panels.description: Wide. The long rectangular courtyard edged with pillared verandahs. On the left, women of the house on woven mats sorting pepper berries, bangles at their wrists, in plain off-white cotton mundu with an upper cloth across the chest and over one shoulder (no stitched blouse, no blue or indigo, no coin necklaces, no armlets). On the right, by a well, boys with short spears and an older man in mid-correction. Every head has turned toward the gate, where Nagoji (rust-red turban) is swinging down from his plain grey gelding and Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat) from his sturdy brown pony.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A stranger. A Maratha. A man who had washed up from Portuguese wreckage, and now arrived on a horse instead of a stretcher.

panels.description: Point of view from the gate down the length of the courtyard. At the far end, alone, stands Padmini Amma: in her fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape, simple gold at her ears and throat, a cream cotton sari in the old Kerala drape with the upper cloth across her chest and over one shoulder, no stitched blouse, hitched above the ankles for walking, one hand resting on a long walking stick. No one else in the foreground.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (small, under his breath)
copy.text: Padmini Amma.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A stick that could have been a staff or a cane, depending on who held it.

panels.description: Mid-shot. Nagoji (rust-red turban, still in his riding boots) inclines his head in a measured bow, not a deep one. Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat, scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw) beside him, open-handed, presenting him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The bow I would have given a landholding Patil at home.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Amma. This is the rider I spoke of. The one the sea and the Portuguese fought over.

panels.description: Insert: where her eyes go. Nagoji's left hand at his belt, the nails healed but ridged. Below the cuff of his cream sleeve, the lower edge of the Portuguese brand, a pale puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading, no letters or numerals, on the left forearm just above the wrist. The belt leather worn pale.

Padmini Amma, close, unhurried: hair coiled at the nape, simple gold, cream cotton drape over one shoulder. Letterer's note: she speaks slow Malayalam, pitched so he can follow; letter it in plain English with no brackets.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The one who survived. The sea spits out strange things.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You understand me, Nagoji?

panels.description: Tight horizontal close-up of Nagoji from the lower edge of the rust-red turban to the chin: level eyes, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, healed lips, small gold ear stud. Flat and steady. He answers in halting Malayalam.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Enough to know when I am being insulted, Amma.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And enough to know when I am being measured.

panels.description: Padmini Amma, close. One corner of her mouth curves. Nothing else moves.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Good. Men who cannot tell the difference do not live long here.

panels.description: A boy of about twelve trots up to take Nagoji's plain grey gelding by the reins, easy and unafraid. The horse snorts once, then goes with him. Nagoji at one edge of frame, letting the reins go; Padmini Amma's stick gesturing at the other edge.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: Come. Leave the horses to the boys.

panels.description: Walking along the shaded verandah. Padmini Amma half a step ahead, her stick tapping the stone. Nagoji beside her, barefoot now; at the verandah step behind them stand his boots, where he left them. Out in the courtyard, Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat) is already deep in talk with one of her stewards.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The king sends you here to be near his capital and his horse. Clever man.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He knows that understanding an estate is as important as understanding a charge.

panels.description: Two-shot, still walking. Padmini Amma not breaking stride, not looking at him. Nagoji, barefoot, a step behind her shoulder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am a soldier. I count men, hooves, distances.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And who owns the land those hooves cross?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Who feeds the men you count? Whose pepper pays for their powder?

panels.description: From behind Nagoji's shoulder, so his face cannot be seen: an open doorway into a cool room. Two young women of the house (plain off-white cotton mundu, upper cloth over one shoulder, no stitched blouse) bent over palm-leaf bundles, counting and tying; one glances up at him. In the near foreground, Padmini Amma in profile, her eyes sliding sideways to him. She has noticed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I smiled at the women a bit longer than I should have.

panels.description: Another doorway: a dim, quiet room holding a wooden chest, a lamp niche, and a sleeping mat rolled against the wall. Padmini Amma at the edge of frame, her stick pointing into it.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: My grandmother slept in that room. Her brother ran away with a dancer. Her sons went to fight for different chiefs.

panels.description: Padmini Amma turning back to him, the room behind her. Nagoji's shoulder and rust-red turban at the near edge of frame.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: This house stayed with her sisters and their daughters.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The men come and go. The name stays here.

panels.description: Nagoji, barefoot on the verandah, reasonable, sure of himself.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: In the Deccan we inherit through the father's line. A man's field is his son's.

panels.description: Low angle along the verandah floor, composed horizontally. In the left foreground, the tip of Padmini Amma's long walking stick striking the polished floor. In the right third, Padmini Amma's face, turned full on him for the first time; he is off panel.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If your son's wife hates you, does that field still feel like safety?

panels.description: Wide. A smaller inner courtyard shaded by a huge jackfruit tree, with a stone platform beneath it worn smooth by generations. Padmini Amma stands by the platform, stick planted. Nagoji (rust-red turban, barefoot) beside her, his head turned toward the low wall behind, over which show the heads and raised sticks of youths training in the kalari, a girl among them.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Kalari. Our boys and some of our girls.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: When the king calls, they are ready. When the king forgets us, they are also ready.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No threat in it. Only a fact, laid on the ground like a tool.

panels.description: Nagoji and Padmini Amma seated on the stone platform. A young woman of the house (plain off-white cotton mundu, upper cloth over one shoulder, no stitched blouse, no blue, no coin necklace) sets down brass tumblers of water, meeting Nagoji's eyes as she does, unhurried. Behind her, a second young woman brings a plate of sliced fruit and fried snacks.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In my village, women moved like shadows at the edge, leaving food and vanishing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here they flowed through the centre, talking, laughing, listening in.

panels.description: Padmini Amma and Nagoji on the platform, the young women gone. She bites into a slice of jackfruit as she speaks, the juice shining on her fingers, a cloth ready in her other hand. Nagoji answering, level.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The king has not yet decided whether you are a spear for his hand or a knife that might cut it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am still an experiment. He told me so himself.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He is honest, then. Good.

panels.description: Nagoji, close. The question has found him somewhere unguarded.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: You have a family. Back in your hills.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The word tasted heavier than jackfruit.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Parents. A younger brother. Some fields that do not know whether I am alive.

panels.description: Small inset, bottom right. Padmini Amma wiping her fingers on the cloth, eyes on him, casual.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And a wife?

panels.description: Nagoji, caught off guard, a brass tumbler of water stopped halfway to his mouth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: Why not?

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the Deccan, such a question from a woman I had just met would have been unthinkable.

panels.description: Nagoji looking out past the tree, somewhere north. Behind his head, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame, desaturated: a column of Maratha horsemen riding at dawn across open country toward a whitewashed Portuguese fort wall with low bastions, a plain saffron pennant at its head, the riders small and distant. No devices on the pennant, no text.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I rode where the Peshwa's orders sent me.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not think it fair to ask a woman to wait for a man who might ride into Portuguese guns one morning and never ride back.

panels.description: Padmini Amma, dry as dust, prying a seed out of a jackfruit bulb with her thumb and flicking it off the edge of the platform.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You assume she would wait.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Here, if a man does not return, the house continues. Perhaps your hills should learn from that.

panels.description: Wide and high, looking down into the inner courtyard. Nagoji on the platform, head tipped back in one short, surprised laugh, and the sound sends crows flapping up out of the jackfruit tree. Padmini Amma beside him, unmoved. At a far doorway, a woman of the house (plain off-white cotton mundu and upper cloth) turns to look.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You speak freely, Amma.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I own this land. Why should I not?

panels.description: Padmini Amma, close, studying him. A decision made behind her eyes.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You will hear a word here. *Sambandham.*

panels.description: Tall panel, about a third of the page. Padmini Amma and Nagoji (rust-red turban, barefoot) seated facing each other on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree. Padmini's stick draws a line on the stone between them: her side, his side. She is mid-gesture, not lecturing.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: An equal bond. Not ownership. Not conquest.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: A woman stays in her own house. Her *tharavadu.* The man comes to her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He does not own the house. He does not own the land. He does not own her.

panels.description: Over the low wall again: the kalari youths, sweat-shining, sticks crossed. Padmini Amma's stick points toward them past Nagoji's shoulder; Nagoji in the foreground, turned to look.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the children?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Belong to her line. The father is honoured. Loved, often.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But he is a guest in the house where his children grow.

panels.description: Nagoji, searching for a word in a language he only half has, one hand turning in the air. Padmini Amma at the edge of frame, her stick lifted to cut him off.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It sounds... complicated.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: It sounds practical. A man who goes to war may not return.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: In your system, his wife and children are ruined. In ours, they are exactly where they were before.

panels.description: Close on Padmini Amma, leaning toward him, smiling, showing teeth.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: We do not pretend men are reliable, Sawant. We plan for their failures.

panels.description: Two-shot on the platform. Nagoji leaning in, pushing back. Padmini Amma's smile gone, her face flat, her stick planted upright beside her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if a woman wishes to leave? To follow her husband to his house?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Then she is a fool.

panels.description: Over Padmini Amma's shoulder as she sits back against the trunk of the jackfruit tree, through a gap in the far wall to the green paddy beyond, where two boys of the house are leading Nagoji's plain grey gelding and the other horses of his party out to graze. Nagoji at the edge of frame, following her look.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Your horses will graze in our fields. You will ride from this gate when the king calls.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: That makes you part of this house's story, whether you like it or not.

panels.description: Close on Padmini Amma, leaning forward, her voice gone flat and hard, and the camera comes in with her. Nagoji's face at the edge of frame. Soft in the background, a young woman of the house (plain off-white cotton mundu and upper cloth) crosses the courtyard with a water pot on her hip.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And tell your men to stay away from the girls in the house.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If they try anything, we will carve them from navel to feet. Do not test us on this.

panels.description: Nagoji, not smiling now, his eyes moving past her through the passage to the outer yard, where Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat) stands with a steward beside a baggage cart and two riders of Nagoji's column are unloading saddlebags.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Houses have long memories.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: And longer tongues.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: You will meet one of those tongues soon.

panels.description: Padmini Amma easing back against the trunk, almost amused again. Only Padmini Amma in frame.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: A princess of our Velinadu kin. Revathi Bayi.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: She has more opinions than I have pepper vines.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If you truly want to understand this kingdom, listen to her as carefully as you listen to Ramayyan.

panels.description: Two-shot under the jackfruit tree: Nagoji and Padmini Amma on the stone platform. On her answer she lays her stick across her knees, and her expression shifts, just enough to be seen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had heard the name on the road south. A sharp-tongued royal woman who refused to act grateful when Europeans bowed.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: She supports the king?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: She supports Travancore. Not always the same thing as supporting its current occupant.

panels.description: Large, a third of the page. Padmini Amma in the foreground, speaking to someone off panel. Behind her, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame, desaturated and dissolving into her background: Marthanda Varma in the coastal hall, on his low wooden platform. Tall, bare-chested, one cream-and-gold cloth over the shoulder, gold necklaces, a cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest, Vaishnavite lines on his forehead, no crown, a spear at his shoulder, a map open on the mat before him, a sword within reach.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In my world, such a man expected his nobles to fall in line or fall in the field.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: He allows her to speak against him?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He allows what he cannot easily stop. The Velinadu line is old. Older than his throne.

panels.description: Close on Padmini Amma, her stick held upright before her like a measuring rod, the jackfruit leaves dark behind her. Only Padmini Amma in frame.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The old Eight Houses on the marches once thought themselves kings too, until he broke them.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You outsiders see one crown. We see many, layered on the same land. Sometimes they sit well together. Sometimes they cut.

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji and Padmini Amma on the platform. Beyond the low wall, the kalari rises and falls: the tops of sticks, a youth caught mid-leap. Padmini Amma getting to her feet, using the stick more as a symbol than as a support. Nagoji still seated, looking up at her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: When do we go to Velinadu?

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: In two days. You will come as my guest, not as the king's experiment.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: That will confuse people. Confusion is useful.

panels.description: Padmini Amma standing over him, already turning to go, speaking over her shoulder. Nagoji seated on the platform, his bare feet on the stone in the foreground.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Wash the salt from your skin.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Then we will see whether you can speak to a princess without putting your Deccan boot in your mouth.

panels.description: Wide. Padmini Amma walking away across the main courtyard. The women of the house (plain off-white cotton mundu and upper cloth) part for her without being told and close again behind her; men with account books step aside, then go back to their counting. At the edge of frame, a young girl carrying firewood has paused mid-step to look back toward the jackfruit courtyard, eyes bright.
Wide, high angle, looking down through the jackfruit leaves. Nagoji alone on the stone platform, small in the frame, barefoot, eyes closed. Listening.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In Goa, power had been simple. It carried a crucifix and a gun.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here it sounded like pepper being sifted, like a woman's stick tapping stone.

panels.description: Tight, under the jackfruit tree. An older boy astride a low branch drops a sticky golden bulb of jackfruit into a small child's cupped, waiting hands below. Hands and fruit only; no faces.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king had given me horses and wet sand. Padmini Amma offered something less obvious and perhaps more dangerous.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A house that remembered. A house whose women spoke.

panels.description: Bottom strip. Nagoji's face, close, eyes open again, a rueful half smile. Rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had faced Portuguese interrogations and Arabian Sea storms. Somehow, this felt like the more delicate task.

frames.review_note: v02 fixes the v01 fault: the headland building is gone, leaving only palms, scrub and rock. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust-red turban, red sash, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. He stands in the stirrups with his arm flung out, shouting. His is the only grey horse. The Madurai lancers wear white turbans and ride dark bay and black horses. The Maravar riders are bare-headed on dun and brown ponies, and the line bows. The fishermen are bare-chested in plain white lungis and one is doubled over laughing. The whole upper right is open sky, with room for both captions. Minor notes: the laughing fisherman has no visible shoulder cloth; the lancers wear crossed straps, which the continuity row does not forbid; his ear ornament is hidden. v01 is not acceptable because of the building on the headland.

v02 fixes the v01 faults: the fisherman's lungi is now plain white (it was checked in v01), both men sit cross-legged on a palm-leaf mat with no table, and Nagoji's chin is clean. His eyes are watering and he grins with his mouth open and tongue out. There is no red on his lips or fingers, and the curry stays on the leaf. The lamp is an open clay lamp, and there is a coconut-shell cup of toddy. The fisherman is bare-chested with a cloth over one shoulder.
